title: Nmap — the commands you actually run
inline_answer:
```
# full TCP, then targeted version/script on found ports
nmap -p- --min-rate 2000 -T4 -oN tcp.all TARGET
nmap -p<csv> -sCV -oN tcp.deep TARGET
# top UDP (slow — run in parallel)
nmap -sU --top-ports 50 -oN udp.top TARGET
```

`recon.sh` does this for you with parsing — manual nmap is the fallback when it fails.

title: SMB enumeration (139/445)
inline_answer:
```
nxc smb TARGET -u '' -p ''            # null; then -u guest -p ''
nxc smb TARGET -u U -p P --shares --users --pass-pol
smbclient -N -L //TARGET/            # list shares anon
smbclient -N //TARGET/SHARE          # browse; recurse;prompt;mget *
enum4linux-ng -A TARGET
rpcclient -U '' -N TARGET             # enumdomusers, querydispinfo
```

title: SNMP enumeration (161/UDP)
inline_answer:
```
snmpwalk -v2c -c public TARGET                 # whole tree
snmpwalk -v2c -c public TARGET 1.3.6.1.4.1.77.1.2.25   # users
snmpwalk -v2c -c public TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.4.2.1.2  # processes (creds in args!)
snmp-check TARGET ; onesixtyone -c communities.txt TARGET
```

Try community strings `public`, `private`, `community`, the org name.

title: LDAP enumeration (389/636)
inline_answer:
```
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://TARGET -s base namingcontexts     # find base DN
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://TARGET -b 'DC=corp,DC=com'        # anon dump
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://TARGET -b 'DC=corp,DC=com' '(objectClass=user)' sAMAccountName description
nxc ldap TARGET -u U -p P --users --asreproast a.txt
```

`description` fields frequently hold passwords.

title: FTP (21) — anonymous + enum
inline_answer:
```
ftp TARGET            # anonymous / anonymous  (or anonymous / blank)
# binary; ls -la; recursively grab everything:
wget -m --no-passive ftp://anonymous:anonymous@TARGET
```

Note the banner/version → searchsploit (vsftpd 2.3.4, ProFTPD mod_copy). Check if the FTP root == webroot (upload a shell).

title: Vhost / subdomain fuzzing
inline_answer:
```
ffuf -u http://TARGET/ -H 'Host: FUZZ.domain.com' \
  -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt \
  -fs <baseline_size>          # filter the default-response size
```

Add every discovered vhost to `/etc/hosts`. A different size/code = a real vhost. Also try gobuster `vhost --append-domain`.
